Skip next section Houthi militia attack wounds 11 in Saudi Arabia 08/07/2026 August 7, 2026 Houthi militia attack wounds 11 in Saudi Arabia An attack by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis late on Thursday wounded 11 civilians in southern Saudi Arabia near the Yemeni border, a military official said. The attack injured seven Saudis, two Egyptians, a Yemeni and a Pakistani, according to General Turki al-Maliki, spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition supporting Yemen 's government against the Shiite Houthi rebels. He accused the rebels of "using indiscriminate shelling against civilian objects." Neither the militia or Iran immediately responded to the coalition's statement. Tehran has targeted Saudi Arabia since the US-Iran war started this February, as its regional archrival hosts US military facilities. Less then three weeks ago, the Houthi militants in Yemen declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia , signaling that Riyadh's long-running conflict with the Houthis in Yemen is becoming increasingly intertwined with the wider Middle East war. The pact was "under discussion for a long time," but recent developments in the region accelerated efforts to finalize it, a source close to the Saudi military told AFP. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman was due to meet Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in the Saudi Arabian city. Erdogan was set to arrive on Friday, while Sharif and Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir had already arrived in the kingdom on Thursday. In 2025, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan — the only Muslim-majority country armed with nuclear weapons — announced a joint defense deal . https://english.news.cn/europe/20260825/.text: Minimum wage in Slovakia to rise to 972 euros per month in 2027 BRATISLAVA, Aug. 24 (Xinhua) -- Slovakia's minimum wage will rise to 972 euros (1133.5 U.S. dollars) per month in 2027, up from 915 euros (1067.1 U.S. dollars) in 2026, Slovak Labour, Social Affairs and Family Minister Erik Tomas announced on Monday following a meeting of the tripartite council. "The minimum wage next year will be 972 euros (1133.5 U.S. dollars), bringing it closer to the symbolic threshold of 1,000 euros (1166.2 U.S. dollars)," Tomas said. The minister also presented a qualified estimate for the minimum wage in 2028, when it is expected to exceed 1,000 euros (1166.2 U.S. dollars) per month and could reach 1,016 euros (1184.8 U.S. dollars). Extra payments for night and weekend work will also increase, as they are linked to the minimum wage. The minimum wage in Slovakia is regulated under Act No. 663/2007 Coll. It is set annually for the following calendar year and applies as a monthly and hourly amount. Under the law, the minimum wage is set at 60 percent of the average nominal salary from two years earlier. According to Slovak Statistics Office, the average nominal salary in 2025 stood at 1,620 euros (1889.2 U.S. dollars). Tomas added that approximately 120,000 employees are paid the basic minimum wage in 2026. If all six minimum-wage levels based on job difficulty are taken into account, the measure will affect approximately 160,000 people in 2026, some 6 percent of the country's labor force. ■ News In-depth Sports Business Culture World China Regions Asia & Pacific Europe Middle East North America South America Africa Organizations Services Weather Live & Work in China Doing Business Investment Visit China Study in China More Special Reports Photos Video Corrections About Us Contact Us Media Qiushi Journal Taiwan.cn Youth.cn GMW.cn CE.cn Ecns.cn China Daily CRI.cn China.org.cn People's Daily

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqgm.text: Image source, Getty Images By Caitlin Doherty BBC News Published 15 October 2026 Updated 3 hours ago A Taco Bell cashier's alleged plot for a mass shooting at a Hindu temple near Chicago was thwarted by a tip-off from one of his colleagues, investigators say. Alexandros Paporakis, 19, from Palatine, Illinois, appeared in court on Wednesday charged with one count of making a terrorist threat and one count of unlawful possession of a weapon. Paporakis allegedly sent a message about the planned attack on Sunday to the co-worker, who alerted authorities, officials said. Police said they found writings in which Paporakis identified as a white supremacist and wrote about his hatred for non-white people. Palatine police chief William Nord said on Thursday they were notified about a mass shooting plot on Sunday by someone who had received "concerning electronic communications" from Paporakis. "These communications played a vital role in bringing this matter to the attention of law enforcement," said the police chief. According to CBS, the BBC's US partner, prosecutors said the tipster had worked with Paporakis. Nord said a red Honda RDX registered to Paporakis entered the car park of a "known Hindu temple" in the suburb of Aurora at Sunday lunchtime. The suspect allegedly tried to open fire, but the gun jammed, so he drove home, where he lived with his mother. According to NBC Chicago, Paporakis told his colleague over phone messages that his gun had jammed and he got out of there "super-fast". Once home, he "searched internet trying to learn how to unjam his gun & called a colleague informing them of [his] intent to carry out a mass shooting", reports NBC Chicago. He is thought to have acted alone. The police chief said officers had searched Paporakis' home, where they found a rifle, loaded magazines, hundreds of rounds of rifle ammunition and body armour. Nord said they also discovered an eight-page document by the suspect containing "extremist ideologies" and revealing his plans for an attack. In the writings, he described himself as a "sociopathic white supremacist neo-Nazi", according to CBS. Police have questioned Paporakis' mother, who was said to be unco-operative. The Hindu temple identified by local media as the intended target said it had implemented new security measures. India's Ministry of External Affairs said the incident "adds to growing concerns over racist hostility and anti-India hate in the US". US congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi of Illinois said he was "horrified" by the incident. In a Facebook statement, he said he and his family worship at the temple and were there last Sunday. The Chicago metropolitan area is home to one of the biggest Indian-American populations in the US.
